description: Optimized WHIR schedules for the EVM verifier skeleton (verifier_evm/whir/whir.sol). Trace 2^24, security target 80 bits under the pessimistic (list-decoding-to-capacity) conjecture. These re-balance the stock config_for_80_bits_under_pessimistic_conjecture(24) toward far fewer queries by raising the evaluation-domain rate (LDE factor) and leaning on proof-of-work, which is the right trade for an L1 verifier whose dominant cost is calldata (Merkle openings).
optimizations_applied: Merged the memory(38) and witness(65) base oracles into ONE oracle (103 cols); setup(10) stays separate. Round 0 now opens 2 Merkle trees per query instead of 3 (one fewer path + leaf hash + state root). Allowed because this verifier may dictate a custom commitment layout. TOTAL_ORACLE_COLS unchanged at 113.
First (initial) query round PoW raised to 30 bits.

First-round LDE factor raised from 2 to 16 (variant A) or 32 (variant B). RS-evaluation-domain log2 is then held CONSTANT across all rounds (28 for A, 29 for B), so LDE factors increase automatically as the polynomial folds down, and query counts fall.
Intermediate/final rounds use up to 32 PoW bits where it removes a query.

security_model.regime: pessimistic conjecture (1 verifier bit per query per inverse-rate bit)

fold_steps_note: Unchanged. Sums to 23 = number of opening-point variables. poly_size_log2 per round before folding: [24,23,18,13,8,4]; final remainder = 1 var => FINAL_MONOMIALS_LEN = 2.
rounds_layout: round 0 = initial (2 base oracles), rounds 1..4 = internal, round 5 = final

variant_B_lde32.note: First-round LDE = 32. Constant RS-domain log2 = 29. Fewest queries; preferred for calldata.

variant_C_packed_2pow28.note: NEW LEAF/TREE LAYOUT. Polynomials committed 16x bigger (2^28 instead of 2^24), so the merged memory+witness oracle is 8 polynomials (103 cols padded to 128, grouped 16-per-poly) and setup is 1 polynomial => 9 batched columns total (was 113), over 2 trees. A round-0 leaf holds cols*2^k0 elements; with k0 now VARIABLE the narrow 9-column leaves slash per-query calldata even though WHIR must fold 28 variables and trees are deeper. Schedule found by brute-force search minimizing calldata (the dominant L1 cost), with correct round-0 (2-oracle) costing.
variant_C_packed_2pow28.search_constraints: RS_domain_log2 <= 32, pow_bits <= 30, first fold k0 <= 3, subsequent folds <= 6, security q*log2(lde)+pow >= 80. PoW pinned to 30 every round (free verifier security => always maximal). k0=2 wins (k0=3 grows the round-0 leaf too much; k0=1 leaves too many later rounds).

measured_gas_comparison_2pow24_sec80.note: Skeleton-measured. calldata_gas = EIP-7623 nonzero floor (40 gas/byte). All keccak256, single-root trees.

input_state_packing.note: Input state (transcript seed, batching challenge, opening value, opening point z_initial, base-oracle commitments) is committed as a SINGLE keccak256 stored in one slot. The proof carries the preimage as its first bytes; the verifier hashes it once and checks against the slot (sink). Replaces ~33 cold SLOADs (~69k gas) with 1 SLOAD + 1 keccak, at the cost of ~0.5KB extra calldata.
input_state_packing.measured_effect_packed_single_root: per-slot storage: 62336B / verify 947902 / total 3462342;  preimage: 62912B / verify 888846 / total 3426326  => net -36016 gas (SLOAD saving > +576B calldata).

merkle_caps_packed_2pow24_sec80.note: Cap of 2^CAP_LOG2 hashes per commitment. Path shortens by CAP_LOG2 nodes per query (saves total_paths * CAP_LOG2 sibling words); each commitment grows to CAP*32 bytes (base caps in the preimage, 5 intermediate caps in the proof). PACKED has 50 total paths and 7 commitments, so the optimum is small. Measured on VARIANT=2 with preimage state.
merkle_caps_packed_2pow24_sec80.conclusion: Caps ARE beneficial. cap 8 is optimal (cap 16 is within 0.1%, effectively tied); cap 32 over-pays on commitment size and is worse than cap 8 by ~88k gas though still better than single-root. Best (preimage + cap 8): 59680B / 3.28M total, vs 62336B / 3.46M for per-slot storage + single root (~5.4% saving).

variant_D_fully_packed_1column_2pow31.note: MOST-packed option: the 113 witness/memory polys are packed into ONE poly of size 2^(24+ceil(log2 113)) = 2^31 (one column, one tree). A full RS code is computed over 2^31 and the proximity check folds 31 variables. Leaf = 1 column * 2^k0 (tiny), 1 path/query. Implemented as VARIANT=3 (with preimage + cap 8). Verified by build+run, lockstep.
variant_D_fully_packed_1column_2pow31.key_effect: V jumps to 31, so round 0's poly is 2^31. Under RS_domain <= 2^32 the round-0 LDE is FORCED to 2 (31+1=32) => 50 queries in round 0, which dominates. The tiny 1-column leaves do NOT compensate. Beneficial only if the RS-domain cap is relaxed (larger RS code = more prover work, which the user deems acceptable).
variant_D_fully_packed_1column_2pow31.conclusion: Batching all the way to 1 column trades prover RS-domain size for verifier proof size. Under the stated 2^32 RS cap it LOSES (5.11M vs 3.28M for the 8-column V=28 layout) because V=31 forces 50 round-0 queries. It only wins once the RS cap is relaxed: ~2.90M at 2^34 (4x prover domain), ~2.32M at 2^36 (16x prover domain). So 'achievable' gas depends entirely on the tolerated RS-domain blowup.

packing_width_sweep_2pow24_sec80.note: One tree of W columns (witness+memory+setup all packed together, 123 cols padded to 128 => 2^31 total), V = 31 - log2(W), 1 Merkle path/query. RS cap 2^32, cap-8 commitments, hashed-state preimage. MEASURED in the skeleton; calldata matches the DP exactly at every width.
packing_width_sweep_2pow24_sec80.tradeoff: Smaller W = more packing = larger V = round-0 LDE capped lower (32-V) => more round-0 queries. Larger W = wider leaves but fewer round-0 queries. Round-0 queries = ceil(50/(32-V)).
packing_width_sweep_2pow24_sec80.conclusion: Among {1,2,4,8} the ranking is monotonic: 8x2^28 best, 1x2^31 worst (each less-packed step cuts gas because it relieves RS-cap pressure on round 0; queries 50->25->17->13). Packing harder toward 1 column is the WRONG direction under the 2^32 RS cap. Global optimum is W=16 (~2.51M), flat to W=32. Also: one-tree (setup merged in) beats the earlier two-tree VARIANT 2 by ~0.55M (one fewer path/query).

ram_constraint_140GB.note: Prover must hold the round-0 RS-encoded oracle in RAM. Total original data = 2^31 elements (16 bytes each, BabyBear quartic), so the round-0 oracle = W * 2^(V+lde0) * 16 = 2^(35+lde0) bytes, INDEPENDENT of packing width W (W*2^V is fixed at 2^31). Later rounds hold 1 column => 2^(RS_domain)*16 bytes.
ram_constraint_140GB.under_140GB: round-0 LDE capped at x4 (lde0<=2) => round-0 queries >= 25; later-round RS-domain capped at 2^33. The 8x2^28-with-RS-2^32 (0.5TB) option is INFEASIBLE.

packing_width_options_at_140GB_measured.note: MEASURED exactly; best, but only marginally

ram_constraint_140GB.packing_conclusion: Under 140GB the packing width barely matters: round-0 queries are RAM-pinned at 25 for every W, so all of {1,2,4,8}x give ~3.37-3.43M (8x2^28 marginally best). The width that mattered without RAM (8-16x) no longer does.
ram_constraint_140GB.pow_lever: When RAM caps round-0 LDE, the other knob to cut round-0 queries is PoW: q0 = ceil((80-pow)/lde0). At 140GB (lde0=2): pow30->25q, pow40->20q, pow50->15q, pow60->10q. Trades prover grind (2^pow hashes) for verifier proof size when RAM blocks a bigger LDE; PoW costs the verifier ~1 hash regardless.
ram_constraint_140GB.summary: RAM directly buys round-0 LDE (each RAM doubling => +1 LDE bit => ~halves round-0 queries => ~0.5M gas). At 140GB the achievable WHIR verifier gas is ~3.37M (vs 2.45M at 512GB / x16 LDE, vs 2.73M unconstrained-best). Packing width is nearly irrelevant under RAM pressure; raising PoW above 30 is the only further lever without more RAM.

tradeoffs.verifier_win: Far fewer queries => fewer Merkle openings => much smaller calldata (the dominant L1 cost) and less verifier hashing/mulmod. Variant A ~37 queries, Variant B ~31 queries, vs stock 99.
tradeoffs.prover_cost: Holding rs_domain at 2^28/2^29 means EVERY round commits an oracle over a 2^28/2^29 domain (stock middle rounds were 2^27, base was 2^25). Expect ~2-4x more prover FFT/commit work. PoW grind rises to 2^30..2^32 per round (stock was 2^10..2^28).
tradeoffs.depth_note: Merkle depths shown assume a SINGLE bytes32 root per commitment (skeleton model). With the production CAP_SIZE=16 cap, subtract 4 from every depth.
